episodes.title: Whipping death of a farm laborer in Lincoln County, Georgia
episodes.summary: Two sons of planter Joseph Dill whipped a Black laborer who had returned to Canady's farm to demand his wages, inflicting 500 lashes. He died shortly afterward. An inquest ruled it murder, but the grand jury ignored the bill.

episodes.title: Lynching of Tom Tarver
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A band of about 50 disguised Ku Klux entered Dalton after midnight, whipped women at Jane Kidd's house, beat Tom Carver to death after torture, badly beat Armstead, and ordered several people to leave town. The second account adds shots exchanged and a demolished house.

episodes.title: Whipping of Richard Hindsman
episodes.summary: White citizens of Villa Rica, Georgia, whipped a colored man with three hundred lashes for insulting a white woman. The paper condemns the citizens' usurping of judge, jury and sheriff.

episodes.title: Lynching of Peter Stamps
episodes.summary: A mob at Douglasville, Georgia, lynched Peter Stamps, a Black man, for an alleged rape of Ada Abercrombie, aged 15. The girl had died shortly before from poison; whether murder or suicide is not known.

episodes.title: Canton, Texas, night shootings (1885)
episodes.summary: A reported war of races in Van Zandt County: whites raided Negro houses in Canton, considerable shooting occurred, a Negro church was burned in the southern part of the county, and two Negroes were killed.

episodes.title: Whipping of Jim Caskey
episodes.summary: Forty masked men took Jim Caskey, a Black man, from his home near Douglass Church in Newberry County, gave him 200 lashes and ordered him to leave the county within twenty-four hours. The party also went to Lee Clinton's house, but he was absent.

episodes.title: Lynching of Ross Hollis
episodes.summary: A mob lynched Ross Hollis, a Black soldier said to be the assassin of Dr. Lynch, at Sturgis. Armed Black soldiers from Fort Meade then threatened to burn the town until a 7th cavalry patrol secured it and returned them to post.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Figures and Cicero Green
episodes.summary: One hundred mounted, armed men entered Minden, Louisiana, on the night of July 21 and killed two Negroes confined in the jail. They took prisoner every citizen who appeared, including editor Moses Fort, who was released after several hours.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jake Evans
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A mob overpowered officers who had arrested Jake Evans, a Black man said to have assaulted a white woman, and hanged him to a tree at Auburn, Alabama. Date is not given; placed by issue date.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Embry, Johnson and Hanesford
episodes.summary: On Saturday night a mob planned to hang the jailed Negro boys Embry, Johnson and Hanesford. Colored men offered to guard the jail, and the judge had the prisoners removed.

episodes.title: Lynching of Henry Davis
episodes.summary: At 4 a.m. about 100 masked men demanded Henry Davis, a 19-year-old Black man held for assaulting a girl, from the Cuthbert jail. The jailer refused, the crowd broke in, and they hanged Davis to a railroad bridge rafter and riddled him with bullets.

episodes.title: Whipping of Samuel Low and West Regan
episodes.summary: Seven disguised men visited the home of Samuel Low, Black, in Duck River Bottom, Tennessee, took him to the woods and gave him over one hundred blows with iron wood switches. West Regan, Black, was also beaten and ordered to leave the county. Low was seriously hurt.

episodes.title: Killing of a Black man in Humphreys County, Tennessee (1885)
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A crowd intending to beat a Black man in Humphreys County shot him as he tried to escape. His body was found near his cabin the next morning. No perpetrators were found.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of George Mack in Huntingdon, Pennsylvania
episodes.summary: Twelve attaches of Cole's circus, two of them colored, allegedly outraged Bertha Morrison near Huntington, Pa., on a Monday night. She identified colored George Mock, and a lynching was described as imminent. The date is inferred from the article's reporting.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Anderson at Danville, Kentucky
episodes.summary: A mob of about a hundred went to Danville to hang Negro Anderson, accused of the assault on Mrs. J. H. Hiatt; the plan failed. Mr. Hiatt says he pursued Anderson all afternoon.

episodes.title: Waterloo attack on emigration agent John Milam
episodes.summary: A mob carried railway agent I. L. Milan from his hotel in Waterloo County, S.C., whipped him and made him walk several miles through the woods. The white people of the county had threatened to kill the first man who induced Negroes to leave.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jack Hopkins
episodes.summary: A gang of masked men rode into Monticello, fired hundreds of buckshot through the openings of Pauley's patent cell into jailed George Hopkins, who had wounded his employer, and killed him.

episodes.title: Killing of Warren Bennett
episodes.summary: Warren Bennett, a Black youth, was shot twice while picking cotton on Tumblin's place; an inquest returned a verdict against unknown persons, and a warrant against white suspect Wade Bolt was not vigorously pursued.

episodes.title: Turning back of the Elberton colored band from Madison County, Georgia
episodes.summary: A colored band hired by Madison county prohibitionists to play on election day was informed it would possibly receive rough treatment and returned across the river without ceremony.

episodes.title: Lynching of Lawrence
episodes.summary: A company of men hanged a Black man named Lawrence, accused of rape, within the limits of Girard, Kansas. A mass meeting of Baxter Springs citizens approved the hanging and thanked the lynchers; the resolutions also address property damage done in Girard.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Samuel B. Goode
episodes.summary: A crowd surrounded Goode, alias Booker, a Black man said to have killed Policeman North, as he was taken from the Old Slip Station-House to the Tombs, yelling "Lynch him" and "Kill the black hound." He was committed without bail.

episodes.title: Lynching of William Cooper
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A mob in the Seventeenth District of the county went to William Cooper's house, a Black man, and fired several shots, killing him. Jack Allison, a young white man, was hit by buckshot and was expected to die.

episodes.title: Masked-band attack on Wallace Thompson's home in Lee County, Alabama
episodes.summary: A mob of masked men broke into Wallace Thompson's home about four miles from Columbus in Lee County, Alabama, and drove him out. It pursued him and whipped several negroes on his place to force them to reveal his whereabouts.

episodes.title: Shooting of a Black soldier by the Hastings city marshal
episodes.summary: The city marshal of Hastings shot a Black soldier about three weeks before this report; the soldier was recovering and had gone to join his regiment.

episodes.title: Keyport store riot (1885)
episodes.summary: A gang of men from the Big Woods attacked a man in front of a Keyport hotel, then attacked the adjoining store kept by colored people, assaulting the proprietor with a chair and breaking in the store front amid a brickbat melee. Warrants were issued.

episodes.title: Lynching of an unnamed Black man at Oxford, Mississippi (1885)
episodes.summary: A Black man who allegedly attempted an outrage at Oxford, Mississippi, was lynched. The paper gives no date, perpetrators or method.

episodes.title: Lynching of Charles Williams
episodes.summary: Twelve or fifteen unidentified men seized Charles Williams, a Black prisoner under guard for an alleged assault on a white girl, and shot him in the road about five and a half miles from Laurens Court House. The inquest was brief and no report went to the Governor.

episodes.title: Beating of Pearl at the Avondale picnic
episodes.summary: At the B&O employees' picnic at Ayondale, Licking Reservoir, Ohio, on Saturday, a crowd assaulted a colored man named Pearl, who had struck a white man, and beat him terribly.

episodes.title: Whipping of Kate Brown
episodes.summary: Two white men dragged Kate Brown (colored) from the Squire's office at Hillsboro, Caroline County, where they awaited trial for an earlier beating of her, and whipped her again more severely. Bystanders did not help.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Wyatt Jones
episodes.summary: Lynchburg people hunted Wyatt Jones, a Black man accused of raping a 10-year-old girl about a week earlier, intending to lynch him. Black men captured him at pistol point and took him to the sheriff, where he is jailed and reportedly confessed.
